Spiritual Blindness
SPIR-ih-choo-uhl BLYND-nes
noun
From Greek tuphloō (G5186, to blind) and pneumatikos (G4152, spiritual); the inability of the natural man to perceive and receive the things of the Spirit of God.

Biblical Definition

Spiritual blindness is the settled incapacity of the natural, unregenerate man to perceive, understand, and embrace the things of God. The Reformed faith roots this doctrine in total depravity: the fall has not merely wounded man but darkened his understanding, so that the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness unto him, neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned (1 Cor 2:14). This blindness is moral and judicial, not a mere lack of information. The god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ should shine unto them (2 Cor 4:4). The man born blind in John 9 is a living parable of this truth: Christ gives him sight while the seeing Pharisees remain blind, and the Lord declares that for judgment He is come, that they which see not might see, and that they which see might be made blind (John 9:39). Because the bondage is total, the remedy can only be sovereign and supernatural. No argument or moral effort can open blind eyes; only the new birth, the God who commanded light to shine out of darkness shining in the heart, gives the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ (2 Cor 4:6). Spiritual sight is therefore the gift of monergistic grace, and every believer who now sees does so because the Lord opened eyes once shut fast.

Webster 1828 Definition

The natural man's settled inability to perceive the things of God, cured only by the sovereign gift of the new birth.

SPIRITUAL BLINDNESS, noun. From Greek tuphloō (G5186, to blind) and pneumatikos (G4152, spiritual); the incapacity of the natural man to discern divine things.

A moral and judicial darkness, not a mere want of information, rooted in the fall.

The god of this world blinds the minds of unbelievers lest the gospel light shine unto them.

As it is written, 'But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him' (1 Cor 2:14).

Cured only by the new birth, when God who commanded light to shine out of darkness shines in the heart.

Key Scripture

1Co 2:14 — "But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned."

2Co 4:4 — "In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them."

Joh 9:39 — "And Jesus said, For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind."

2Co 4:6 — "For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ."

Modern Corruption

Spiritual blindness is corrupted when softened into mere ignorance curable by education or persuasion, denying the totality of the natural man's inability.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The persistent error is doctrinal: to recast spiritual blindness as a curable ignorance that the right argument, experience, or program might overcome, leaving the sinner with some native power to choose the light. This denies the plain word that the natural man cannot know the things of God, for they are spiritually discerned.

The principle to recover is total depravity and the monergistic remedy that follows from it. Because the blindness is total and judicial, the cure must be wholly of God, the same Creator who said let there be light shining anew in the darkened heart. Spiritual sight is not coaxed from the sinner but given in the new birth, and every soul that now beholds the glory of God in the face of Christ does so by sovereign grace alone.

Hebrew Roots

Greek tuphloō (G5186) and related terms describe the darkening of the natural man's mind to the things of God.

expand to see more

Greek tuphloō (G5186) — to make blind, used of Satan blinding unbelieving minds

Greek tuphlos (G5185) — blind; the man born blind of John 9 a parable of the soul

Greek psuchikos (G5591) — natural, soulish; the man without the Spirit who cannot discern

Greek pōroō (G4456) — to harden, to make callous, the kindred blinding of the heart

Only palingenesia (G3824), the new birth, gives the blind soul spiritual sight

Usage

"Spiritual blindness is total: the natural man cannot know the things of the Spirit."

"No argument cures spiritual blindness; only the God of creation shining in the heart."

"The man born blind in John 9 pictures the soul to whom Christ alone gives sight."
